title: Pathways and Barriers to Trauma Treatment in Trauma-Related Disorders
summary:
Some people who have experienced distressing or traumatic events develop a trauma-related disorder over the course of their lives, such as Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD). This mental health condition can involve persistent symptoms like nightmares, heightened startle responses, or a feeling of emotional numbness. Although effective treatments for trauma-related disorders exist, many affected individuals do not seek help at all or only do so very late. Furthermore, the wide range of available services can make it difficult to find the right treatment for an individual's specific needs.
Finding appropriate care is often associated with various barriers, both on a personal level and due to structural factors within the healthcare system. To date, little is known about which services and contact points affected individuals actually turn to on their path through the healthcare system, and in what order they use them.
The aim of this study is therefore to gain a better understanding of the factors that help or hinder people in seeking effective support, as well as to trace the pathways they take through different healthcare services. To this end, we are conducting an anonymous online survey with members of the general population aged 16 and older about their experiences, from their very first point of contact to specialized treatment options. Because both symptoms and available treatments vary greatly from person to person, the findings of this study aim to provide a first step toward matching affected individuals more accurately with suitable support services and making trauma care in Germany more accessible and needs-oriented in the future.
conditions: Reaction to severe stress, and adjustment disorders

interventions.name: Anonymous online survey to assess perceived barriers and facilitators to accessing trauma-focused treatment and pathways through the healthcare system in the general population.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Self-reported traumatic experiences and resulting psychological distress that have led to considering seeking treatment (regardless of whether the participant is currently seeking treatment, currently in treatment, has completed treatment, or discontinued seeking treatment without starting it)

Access to an internet-enabled device and an internet connection to complete the online survey
Exclusion criteria:
Failure to meet the inclusion criteria (no further exclusion criteria apply)
